summary: The bill amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act and Individuals with Disabilities Education Act to bar federal funding for any charter school or its management organization that contracts with a for-profit entity to operate, oversee, or manage the school, while still permitting contracts for ancillary services such as food, transportation, or supplies.

scores.thoughts: The bill regulates the use of existing federal education funds under ESEA and IDEA by prohibiting for-profit contracts for core operations of charter schools. It does not authorize new spending, cut appropriations, or alter overall funding levels—it only imposes conditions on how funds may be spent to prevent profit extraction. This has no direct bearing on expanding or reducing government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection.
The bill addresses only K-12 education funding and charter school governance; it has no connection to healthcare policy or delivery systems.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues appear in the bill.
The legislation is silent on immigration, border policy, visas, or related protections.
No provisions address reproductive rights, abortion access, or funding restrictions related to abortion.
The bill does not mention or affect military or defense budgets or policy.
No environmental, climate, or regulatory provisions are present.
The bill does not alter welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.

The bill directly amends ESEA and IDEA to bar charter schools and their management organizations from contracting with for-profit entities for core operations (curriculum, budget, staffing, etc.), while permitting only ancillary service contracts. This strengthens nonprofit requirements and federal accountability standards for publicly funded charter schools, limiting profit-driven privatization models. It therefore aligns with greater public oversight and federal involvement in education rather than expanded school choice or privatization.
No drug-related enforcement, decriminalization, or policy changes are addressed.
The bill contains no criminal justice, sentencing, or policing provisions.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures are included.
The legislation does not address deficits, debt reduction, or federal borrowing.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
Foreign aid is not mentioned or affected.
The bill has no connection to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or oversight provisions exist.
The bill does not address union rights, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
No religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination measures are included.
